newsitem.title: KENYA: Ugandan tea complaint sent to Kenya government.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan tea complaint sent to Kenya government.

text.p: East African Tea Trade Association officials are trying to calm down Ugandan exporters after complaints about sales through the weekly Mombasa tea auction.
A Kenyan tea official who declined to be identified said on Saturday the problems raised by Ugandan exporters last week had been forwarded to the government for resolution.
Uganda Tea Authority General Manager Mary Mugabi said last week the biggest problem for Ugandan tea exports was the cost of them being held in bonded warehouses before auction in Mombasa.
The Uganda Tea Association, the main buyer's group, last month complained Kenya had a deliberate policy of undermining foreign teas and asked the Kenyan government to intervene.
It said it took time to clear the tea from warehouses and extra costs amounted to some two U.S. cents per kg.
Landlocked Uganda sells about 70 percent of its tea through the Mombasa auction.
The Kenyan official said the bottleneck which was upsetting the Ugandans was a Kenya Revenue Authority requirement for all foreign teas but the issue had been taken up with authorities.
"We need Ugandans and the Ugandans need us. We shall do all that is possible to reach a logical end," said the official.
